svg.title: How one MUbind training example is prepared
svg.desc: The data loader prepares each training example on the fly. Step 1 reads one stored protein, here a real 53-residue training protein, as amino-acid letters, 3Di structure letters and three properties, length, charge and hydrophobicity. Step 2 encodes it on a 70-position canvas, where every position becomes a column of 8 numbers, 6 for the amino acid and 2 for its 3Di letter, and the 17 positions after the protein are zeros. Step 3 hides part of it. A random design task picks residues to redesign, here two stretches, and some 3Di hints and properties are hidden too, here the 3Di of the second stretch and the charge. The prepared training example holds what the model is given and the complete protein it learns to produce.
svg.text: How one training example is prepared
Each time a protein is drawn for training, it becomes a fill-in-the-blanks exercise. The model sees part of it and learns to produce the rest.
Each stored row holds one protein as amino-acid letters, the matching 3Di structure letters and three properties.
Every position on a 70-position canvas becomes a column of 8 numbers, 6 for the amino acid and 2 for its 3Di letter.
Positions after the protein are all zeros. The shading shows this protein's real values, darker is larger.
A random design task picks the residues the model must redesign. Their 3Di hints and some properties may be hidden too.
Here two stretches are redesigned. Other draws keep only one end, keep a middle piece, or redesign the whole protein.
each cell stands for its column of 8 numbers
the complete protein, with the redesigned positions dark
A real training protein with one illustrative draw
